_meta.note: Pass/fail against the five hard filters in profiles.json. `false` needs a reason; measured failures cite the benchmark. Applied before any weighting.
_meta.legend: mpw = multi_process_write, mnt = maintained, shs = self_hostable, fit = fits_small_vps, sor = store_of_record

markdown-files.reason: mpw: no atomic read-modify-write across processes; two agents updating one note is last-writer-wins

sqlite-begin-concurrent.reason: mnt: an unmerged experimental branch of SQLite; shipping it means maintaining a custom build indefinitely

hctree.reason: mnt: experimental, no stable on-disk format, no release date

duckdb.reason: mpw: MEASURED — 7 of 8 writer processes could not open the database file at all (rmw workload, connect errors); only one process ever writes

pglite.reason: mpw: single process, single connection by design

kuzu.reason: mnt: acquired by Apple Oct 2025, repository archived. mpw: single writer

rust-embedded-kv.reason: mpw: redb/sled/fjall allow one process to hold the file read-write; RocksDB likewise

lancedb.reason: mpw: MEASURED — 822 of 1600 read-modify-write updates lost at 8 writers, with zero errors reported. No atomic update primitive exists to use instead

chroma.reason: mpw: embedded mode is single-process. sor: a vector index, not a state store

milvus-lite.reason: fit: standalone needs etcd + object storage, ~500 MB idle. mpw: Lite is single-process

ann-libraries.reason: sor: an index in RAM with no durability or concurrency; it is a component of a database, not one

qdrant.reason: sor: MEASURED — no transactional primitive; set_payload read-modify-write loses updates. Excellent as a retrieval index beside a state store

typesense-meili.reason: sor: a search index, explicitly not a system of record

elasticsearch.reason: fit: ~1.2 GB idle JVM. sor: near-real-time refresh breaks read-your-own-write

clickhouse.reason: sor: no transactions and no efficient row updates; mutable agent state is the wrong shape for it

tidb-cockroach.reason: fit: a Raft cluster needs ~2 GB before it does anything useful

nats-jetstream.reason: sor: no query capability at all — you cannot ask it a question about the data it holds

kafka-redpanda.reason: fit: ~500 MB idle. sor: a log, not a queryable store

neo4j-memgraph-falkor.reason: fit: ~700 MB idle for Neo4j; FalkorDB is lighter but still a second daemon for a few thousand notes

sync-layers.reason: sor: a replication layer over Postgres — it presupposes the answer rather than being one

crdt.reason: sor: converges without choosing a winner, so task claims and counters are structurally unrepresentable

foundationdb.reason: fit: cluster overhead. sor: a substrate you build a database on, with a 5-second transaction limit

managed-rds.reason: shs: writes require the network; violates the charter rule that every dependency is a local process or file

turso-cloud.reason: shs: writes go to the cloud authority

mem0.reason: sor: a policy layer that still requires you to choose the database underneath it

zep-graphiti.reason: sor: same — a memory framework over a backing store, and its preferred backend (Kuzu) is archived

letta.reason: sor: owns the agent loop, which collides with Jod's 'harnesses think, Jod delegates' rule
